as_of: Current T20I rankings reflect all matches up to and including South Africa v Zimbabwe, 06 September 2026 (per iccbackup.co.uk current-rankings pages). Best-ever/peak tables are all-time and each entry carries its own career-best date/year.
notes: Ratings are ICC 0-1000 player-rating points. PEAK tables (test_bat_best, test_bowl_best, odi_bat_best, odi_bowl_best, t20i_bat_best, t20i_bowl_best) are the ICC 'best-ever / career-best rating' lists, 100 entries each, scraped from iccbackup.co.uk (a long-standing mirror of the official ICC/Reliance ICC Rankings all-time feed; icc-cricket.com itself renders its tables client-side and returns no data to a plain fetch). Every one of the top ~26 Test batting and top ~26 Test bowling rows, and the top 10 ODI batting/bowling rows, were cross-checked against the cited tables in the Wikipedia article 'ICC Men's Player Rankings' and matched exactly (Bradman 961, Smith 947, Hutton 945, Hobbs/Ponting 942, Barnes 932, Lohmann 931, Imran 922, Muralitharan 920, Garner 940, Viv Richards 935 ODI, etc.). The 'date' on peak rows is the date the career-best rating was achieved, as given by the source. CAVEAT: the source dates Bradman's 961 to 22/08/1934, while Wikipedia/most secondary sources give 1948 - the rating value 961 is agreed, the date is not. ALL-ROUNDER PEAK LISTS: the ICC never published a deep all-time all-rounder list (confirmed via Wayback CDX of relianceiccrankings.com - only /alltime/{test,odi,t20}/{batting,bowling} ever existed; the icc-cricket.com pages titled 'all-time all-rounder' actually show current standings). test_ar_best (10 rows, peak >=500) and odi_ar_best (11 rows) are therefore taken verbatim from the ICC-cited tables in the Wikipedia article and are the complete published lists, not truncations. T20I ALL-ROUNDER CURRENT is only 10 rows: every accessible source caps the all-rounder list (iccbackup renders top 10, Cricbuzz top 15, icc-cricket.com is JS-only); the 10 rows match Wikipedia's current top 10 exactly. t20i_bat_current and t20i_bowl_current are the top 50 of a fetched top-100 list; their top 10 match Wikipedia's current tables exactly (Ishan Kishan 910, Rashid Khan 753). Bonus keys t20i_bat_best / t20i_bowl_best (100 rows each, peak) were also collected. Source typos 'Mohammad Mohammad Nabi'/'Mohammad Mohammad Rizwan' were normalised to 'Mohammad Nabi'/'Mohammad Rizwan'; Muralitharan is spelled 'Muralidaran' in the Test bowling source. Country codes were expanded to full names. Shared ranks indicate ties. No figure here was estimated, interpolated or invented.
